title: Pin The Dev JSX Runtime So A Cached Chunk Cannot Break Hydration
userRequest: I'm confused about why we are merging main into staging and not the other way around - can you explain this to me? but yes merge it
description:
Declared `react/jsx-dev-runtime` and `react/jsx-runtime` in `optimizeDeps.include`, fixing a `TypeError: jsxDEV is not a function` that killed every React island on /admin — StagingBar, EntryListSearch, AuthGate and AccountMenu all failed to hydrate.

The cause was not the code and not a stale tab, and the first two diagnoses were wrong. The dev server was healthy: NODE_ENV unset so the config's guard fired, the on-disk chunk bundled `react-jsx-dev-runtime.development.js` and assigned `exports.jsxDEV` unconditionally, it was served 200 as `text/javascript` through the browser's exact authenticated proxy path, and a cold headless browser hydrated and responded to a real click. Only one browser profile failed.

The answer was in the response headers: Vite serves optimized deps as `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000,immutable` under a `?v=<browserHash>` URL, and that hash is DETERMINISTIC. A browser had cached the chunk from a window when the deps were optimized under NODE_ENV=production — where `exports.jsxDEV = void 0` — and because re-optimizing reproduces the identical URL, nothing invalidates it. No reload revalidates an immutable subresource, which is why 'hard reload' was bad advice and why clearing `node_modules/.vite/deps` changed nothing: the rebuilt chunk was byte-identical and got the same hash.

`browserHash` derives from `configHash`, so touching the include list is what moves the URL. It went 5110d5f7 → fab1913a, retiring every poisoned copy for everyone rather than asking each person to run a devtools ritual. Declaring the runtimes also buys the reason they are worth pinning on their own merits: both were previously DISCOVERED, so they were optimized part-way through a session under whatever NODE_ENV happened to hold at that instant — which is the window that poisons a cache in the first place. Declared entries are optimized once at startup under the already-corrected env. The comment in astro.config.mjs records the cache-bust lever so the next person hitting this does not have to re-derive it.

A hydration mismatch was revealed underneath, and is deliberately NOT fixed here: the preview proxy rewrites `href="/admin/…"` to `href="/__codeyam_preview/admin/…"` in the rendered HTML, while `EntryListSection` calls `withBase()` at render time and re-computes the unprefixed URL client-side from `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`. The app is self-consistent; the proxy mutates output after render and the client cannot know. Fixing it here would mean teaching production URL-building about a dev tool's path prefix, which would break the deployed site's links. It is a codeyam-editor proxy issue, it affects any island computing URLs at render time, and it is harmless on this project — /admin ships only to dev and the gated review track, and hydration completes regardless.
